newsitem.title: USA: World Bank chief upbeat on job, denies quitting.
newsitem.headline: World Bank chief upbeat on job, denies quitting.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn voiced optimism that he was finally making headway in reforming the organisation and stoutly denied reports that he was planning to leave the job.

"There's a big change going on at the Bank," he told reporters ahead of the International Monetary Fund/World Bank annual meeting. "I am personally of the belief that in another year or two, you'll see immense differences."
He said he was much more optimistic than he was six months ago when he complained to Bank senior staff of the difficulties he faced changing the organisation's culture.
Wolfensohn is trying to shift the Bank's focus away from the quantity of its loans to developing countries toward the quality and effectiveness of its credits and other services.
"Quantity doesn't make the difference," he said. "It's the quality and the effectiveness of what you do."
Wolfensohn called "preposterous" a Business Week magazine report that he was lobbying for a job in the Clinton administration and planned on leaving the World Bank.
